Appendix A
The spinor formalism of the
ISO(5,1)
generators

Let us first review the generators of the Poincaré group,
ISO(3,1)
, which include
L_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu}_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}\sigma^{\nu}_{\beta\dot{\beta}}=\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\widetilde{L}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}+{\tilde{\epsilon}}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}L_{\alpha\beta}
and
P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}
. For massive particles, they are

\displaystyle P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle p_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}+\eta_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}=\lambda_{\alpha}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}+\eta_{\alpha}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}},

(298)

\displaystyle L_{\alpha\beta}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-i\left(\lambda_{\alpha}^{I}\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda^{\beta I}}+\lambda_{\beta}^{I}\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda^{\alpha I}}\right)=-2i\left(\lambda_{(\alpha}\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda^{\beta)}}+\eta_{(\alpha}\frac{\partial}{\partial\eta^{\beta)}}\right),

(299)

\displaystyle{\widetilde{L}}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-i\left(\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{I}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tilde{\lambda}^{\dot{\beta}I}}+\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\beta}}^{I}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tilde{\lambda}^{\dot{\alpha}I}}\right)=-2i\left(\tilde{\lambda}_{(\dot{\alpha}}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tilde{\lambda}^{\dot{\beta})}}+\tilde{\eta}_{(\dot{\alpha}}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tilde{\eta}^{\dot{\beta})}}\right).

(300)

In the spinor-helicity formalism, the commutators are

\displaystyle[L_{\alpha\beta},L_{\gamma\delta}]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle i(\epsilon_{\gamma\beta}L_{\beta\delta}+\epsilon_{\delta\beta}L_{\alpha\gamma}+\epsilon_{\gamma\alpha}L_{\beta\delta}+\epsilon_{\delta\alpha}L_{\beta\gamma}),

(301)

\displaystyle{[{\widetilde{L}}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}},{\widetilde{L}}_{\dot{\gamma}\dot{\delta}}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-i({\tilde{\epsilon}}_{\dot{\gamma}\dot{\beta}}{\widetilde{L}}_{\dot{\beta}\dot{\delta}}+{\tilde{\epsilon}}_{\dot{\delta}\dot{\beta}}{\widetilde{L}}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\gamma}}+{\tilde{\epsilon}}_{\dot{\gamma}\dot{\alpha}}{\widetilde{L}}_{\dot{\beta}\dot{\delta}}+{\tilde{\epsilon}}_{\dot{\delta}\dot{\alpha}}{\tilde{M}}_{\dot{\beta}\dot{\gamma}}),

(302)

\displaystyle{[P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},L_{\beta\gamma}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle i(\epsilon_{\alpha\gamma}P_{\beta\dot{\alpha}}+\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}P_{\gamma\dot{\alpha}}),

(303)

\displaystyle{[P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},\widetilde{L}_{\dot{\beta}\dot{\gamma}}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-i(\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\gamma}}P_{\alpha\dot{\beta}}+\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}P_{\alpha\dot{\gamma}}),

(304)

and the two Casimir operators are

\displaystyle P^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\tilde{m}m=\mathbf{m}^{2},

(305)

\displaystyle W^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{1}{8}{P}^{2}(\mathrm{Tr}[L^{2}]+\mathrm{Tr}[\widetilde{L}^{2}])-\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{Tr}[{P}^{\intercal}LP\widetilde{L}].

(306)

The extended
SO(2)\times ISO(3,1)
still contains the two Casimir operators above, as well as an additional Casimir operator
D_{-}
.
These Casimir operators acting on an arbitrary particle state of the representation
(t,s)
gives

\displaystyle P^{2}|\mathbf{p},t,s,h\rangle

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\mathbf{p}^{2}|\mathbf{p},t,s,h\rangle,

(307)

\displaystyle W^{2}|\mathbf{p},t,s,h\rangle

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-s(s+1)\mathbf{p}^{2}|\mathbf{p},t,s,h\rangle,

(308)

\displaystyle D_{-}|\mathbf{p},t,s,h\rangle

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle t|\mathbf{p},t,s,h\rangle.

(309)

The Casimir operators, along with their eigenvalues, uniquely label a representation of
SO(2)\times ISO(3,1)
. We can thus obtain the corresponding representations by solving the eigenfunctions. The helicity-chirality states introduced in subsection
2.3
span a linear space for each pair
(t,h)
, allowing us to use them as an eigenbasis for the
W^{2}
operator.
For example, eq. (
98
) contains two
(t,h)=(0,0)
states, spanning a dim-2 linear space.
W^{2}
acting on eq. (
98
) gives

\displaystyle W^{2}\begin{pmatrix}\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}+\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-2(2\lambda\cdot\eta)&0\\
0&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}+\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix},

(310)

separating the spin-1 and spin-0 states.

The Lorentz algebra spanned by the generators

L_{\mu\nu}

can be extended to
SO(5,1)
, which is isomorphic to the 4D conformal algebra, by introducing the transversality generators
\{T^{\pm},D_{-}\}
. The key feature of the conformal algebra lies in the commutators, which are

\displaystyle[(T^{+})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},(T^{-})_{\beta\dot{\beta}}]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-\frac{i}{2}(\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\tilde{L}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}+\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}L_{\alpha\beta})-\frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}D_{-},

(311)

\displaystyle{[D_{-},{(T^{\pm})}_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\pm{(T^{\pm})}_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},

(312)

\displaystyle{[L_{\beta\gamma},(T^{\pm})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}}]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-i\epsilon_{\beta\alpha}(T^{\pm})_{\gamma\dot{\alpha}}-i\epsilon_{\gamma\alpha}(T^{\pm})_{\beta\dot{\alpha}}.

(313)

After a suitable redefinition, all the generators can be written into a 6D antisymmetric matrix

\displaystyle L_{MN}=\left(\begin{array}[]{c|cc}L_{\mu\nu}&L_{\mu 4}&L_{\mu 5}\\
\hline\cr L_{4\nu}&0&L_{45}\\
L_{5\nu}&L_{54}&0\end{array}\right),

where
M,N=0,1,2,3,4,5
. The components of eq. (
A
) are

\begin{split}L_{54}&\equiv D_{-}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}}+\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\left(\lambda_{\alpha}\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda_{\alpha}}+\eta_{\alpha}\frac{\partial}{\partial\eta_{\alpha}}\right),\\
L_{5\mu}&\equiv-i\left(T^{+}_{\mu}-T^{-}_{\mu}\right),\\
L_{4\mu}&\equiv T^{+}_{\mu}+T^{-}_{\mu}.\end{split}

(318)

The algebra defined by the commutators of
\{T^{\pm},D_{-},L\}
can be reorganized into the form of the regular
SO(5,1)
algebra with generators
\{L_{MN}\}
:

[L_{QR},L_{MN}]=i\left(\eta_{QM}L_{NR}-\eta_{QN}L_{MR}-\eta_{RM}L_{NQ}+\eta_{RN}L_{MQ}\right),

(319)

where
\eta_{MN}
is the metric in the 6D spacetime, chosen to be
\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1)
.

Then, we introduce the translation generators
\{P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},m,\tilde{m}\}
to the
SO(5,1)
algebra, extending it to the
ISO(5,1)
algebra defined by the following commutators:

\displaystyle{[P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},{T^{+}}^{\beta}_{\dot{\beta}}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-\tilde{m}\delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}},

(320)

\displaystyle{[P_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},{T^{-}}^{\dot{\beta}}_{\beta}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-m\tilde{\delta}^{\dot{\beta}}_{\dot{\alpha}}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta},

(321)

\displaystyle{[m,{T^{+}}^{\alpha}_{\dot{\alpha}}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-P^{\alpha}_{\dot{\alpha}},

(322)

\displaystyle{[\tilde{m},{T^{-}}^{\dot{\alpha}}_{\alpha}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle P^{\dot{\alpha}}_{\alpha},

(323)

\displaystyle{[m,D_{-}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle m,

(324)

\displaystyle{[\tilde{m},D_{-}]}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-\tilde{m}.

(325)

The 4th and 5th components of a 6D momentum
p_{M}
are defined as

\begin{split}p_{4}=\frac{1}{2}(\tilde{m}+m),\ p_{5}=\frac{i}{2}(\tilde{m}-m).\end{split}

(326)

Therefore, the EOM of the 6D momentum is
p_{M}p^{M}=0
, indicating that the 4D massive particle becomes a massless particle in the extended 6D spacetime. This suggests that the massive 4D amplitudes carry a hidden 6D symmetry.

Appendix B
Massive Dirac/Majorana fermion and massive vector

Usually, people use both
(\frac{1}{2},0)
and
(0,\frac{1}{2})
representations of the
SL(2,\mathbbm{C})
group to describe a massive fermion. This description has four degrees of freedom and is called the Dirac fermion. The helicity states are given by four-component spinors as

\displaystyle u_{h=-\frac{1}{2}}^{D}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda\\
\tilde{\eta}\end{pmatrix},

\displaystyle u_{h=+\frac{1}{2}}^{D}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\eta\\
\tilde{\lambda}\end{pmatrix},

(327)

\displaystyle v_{h=-\frac{1}{2}}^{D}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}-\eta\\
\tilde{\lambda}\end{pmatrix},

\displaystyle v_{h=+\frac{1}{2}}^{D}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda\\
-\tilde{\eta}\end{pmatrix}.

where the superscript
D
represents the Dirac fermion. The massive momentum can be written as

\displaystyle(\mathbf{p}^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}=(p^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}+(\eta^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}=\lambda_{\alpha}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}+\eta_{\alpha}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}.

(328)

The Dirac fermion should satisfy an EOM called the Dirac equation:

\displaystyle\begin{cases}(p^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}\tilde{\eta}^{\dot{\alpha}}=-\tilde{m}^{D}\lambda_{\alpha}\\
(\eta^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}\tilde{\lambda}^{\dot{\alpha}}=\tilde{m}^{D}\eta_{\alpha}\\
\end{cases},\quad\begin{cases}(p^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}\eta^{\alpha}=-m^{D}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}\\
(\eta^{D})_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}\lambda^{\alpha}=m^{D}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\\
\end{cases},

(329)

where the spurion masses are

\displaystyle m^{D}=\langle p\eta\rangle,\quad\tilde{m}^{D}=[\eta p].

(330)

For a spin-
1/2
fermion with momentum
p^{\mu}=(E,P\sin\theta\cos\varphi,P\sin\theta\sin\varphi,P\cos\theta)
, the helicity spinors are chosen to be the eigenstates of the helicity operator
h=\frac{\vec{p}\cdot\vec{\sigma}}{|\vec{p}|}
,

\displaystyle\chi_{h=-}=\binom{-e^{-i\varphi}\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}},\quad\chi_{h=+}=\binom{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}}{e^{i\varphi}\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}.

(331)

At the same time, each chirality can be written as

\displaystyle

\displaystyle h=-\frac{1}{2}:

\displaystyle\lambda_{\alpha}(t=-\frac{1}{2})

\displaystyle=\sqrt{E+P}\chi_{h=-},

\displaystyle\tilde{\eta}_{\alpha}(t=\frac{1}{2})

\displaystyle=\frac{m}{\sqrt{E+P}}\chi_{h=-},

(332)

\displaystyle h=+\frac{1}{2}:

\displaystyle\tilde{\lambda}_{\alpha}(t=\frac{1}{2})

\displaystyle=\sqrt{E+P}\chi_{h=+},

\displaystyle\eta_{\alpha}(t=-\frac{1}{2})

\displaystyle=\frac{m}{\sqrt{E+P}}\chi_{h=+}.

We obtain the helicity states for massive spin-
1/2
fermion:

\displaystyle u_{h=-1/2}=\lambda+\tilde{\eta}\to\begin{pmatrix}\lambda\\
\tilde{\eta}\end{pmatrix},\quad u_{h=+1/2}=\tilde{\lambda}+\eta\to\begin{pmatrix}\eta\\
\tilde{\lambda}\end{pmatrix},

(333)

\displaystyle v_{h=-1/2}=\tilde{\lambda}-\eta\to\begin{pmatrix}-\eta\\
\tilde{\lambda}\end{pmatrix},\quad v_{h=+1/2}=\lambda-\tilde{\eta}\to\begin{pmatrix}\lambda\\
-\tilde{\eta}\end{pmatrix}.

(334)

These are the building blocks for the helicity amplitude calculations.

However, there is another type of massive fermion called the Majorana fermion, which only contains
(\frac{1}{2},0)
or
(0,\frac{1}{2})
representation. For example, we choose
(0,\frac{1}{2})
to represent the massive vector, i.e.
\tilde{\lambda}
and
\tilde{\eta}
. Since the complex conjugate representations
\tilde{\lambda}^{*}
and
\tilde{\eta}^{*}
transform as the
(\frac{1}{2},0)
representation under the
SL(2,\mathbbm{C})
Lorentz group, we can construct the four-component spinor:

\displaystyle u_{h=-\frac{1}{2}}^{M}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\tilde{\lambda}^{*}\\
\tilde{\eta}\end{pmatrix},

\displaystyle u_{h=+\frac{1}{2}}^{M}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\tilde{\eta}^{*}\\
\tilde{\lambda}\end{pmatrix},

(335)

\displaystyle v_{h=-\frac{1}{2}}^{M}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}-\tilde{\eta}^{*}\\
\tilde{\lambda}\end{pmatrix},

\displaystyle v_{h=+\frac{1}{2}}^{M}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\tilde{\lambda}^{*}\\
-\tilde{\eta}\end{pmatrix},

where the superscript
M
represents the Majorana fermion. In this case, the massive momentum can be written as

\displaystyle(\mathbf{p}^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}=(p^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}+(\eta^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}=\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{*}\tilde{\lambda}^{\dot{\beta}}+\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{*}\tilde{\eta}^{\dot{\beta}}.

(336)

Therefore, the momentum of Majorana fermion is always real. We cannot generalize its LG from
SU(2)
or
U(2)
into
SL(2,\mathbbm{C})
or
GL(2,\mathbbm{C})
.

The Majorana fermion should satisfy the EOM other than eq. (
329
),

\displaystyle\begin{cases}(p^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\beta}}=-\tilde{m}^{M}\tilde{\lambda}^{*\dot{\alpha}}\\
(\eta^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\beta}}=\tilde{m}^{M}\tilde{\eta}^{*\dot{\alpha}}\\
\end{cases},\quad\begin{cases}(p^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}\tilde{\eta}^{*\dot{\alpha}}=-m^{M}\tilde{\lambda}^{\dot{\beta}}\\
(\eta^{M})_{\dot{\alpha}}^{\dot{\beta}}\tilde{\lambda}^{*\dot{\alpha}}=m^{M}\tilde{\eta}^{\dot{\beta}}\\
\end{cases}.

(337)

where the spurion masses have a different definition

\displaystyle m^{M}=[p\eta]^{*},\quad\tilde{m}^{M}=[p\eta].

(338)

It means that the spurion mass of a Majorana fermion has a phase rotation, different from the uncharged physical mass
\mathbf{m}
.

The massive vector has three representations of the
SL(2,\mathbbm{C})
Lorentz group:
(1,0)
,
(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})
and
(0,1)
. In analogy to the Dirac fermion, we can use them to define a series of six-component helicity states for massive vectors as

\displaystyle u_{h=-1}^{D}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}\\
-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix},u_{h=0}^{D}=\begin{pmatrix}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}-\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
-\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix},u_{h=+1}^{D}=\begin{pmatrix}\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix}.

(339)

For
h=0
, we eliminate the
s=0
state

\displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}m\epsilon_{\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}+\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\tilde{m}\epsilon_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix}.

(340)

Only the state with transversality
0
generates the Goldstone boson. The states with
t=\pm 1
become subleading at high energy.

For helicity
+1
, the EOM is

\displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}0&\eta_{\alpha_{2}\dot{\alpha}_{2}}&0\\
p_{\alpha_{2}\dot{\alpha}_{2}}&0&\eta_{\alpha_{1}\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\\
0&p_{\alpha_{1}\dot{\alpha}_{1}}&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\tilde{\lambda}_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\alpha_{2}}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\tilde{m}&0&0\\
0&\tilde{m}+m&0\\
0&0&m\\
\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
\tilde{\lambda}_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\alpha_{2}}\end{pmatrix}.

(341)

For helicity
0
, the EOM is

\displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}0&(p+\eta)_{\alpha_{2}}^{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}&0\\
(p+\eta)_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}^{\alpha_{2}}&0&(p+\eta)_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}^{\alpha_{1}}\\
0&(p+\eta)_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}^{\alpha_{1}}&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}-\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
-\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix}

(342)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}\tilde{m}&0&0\\
0&\tilde{m}+m&0\\
0&0&m\\
\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}-\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\\
-\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}\end{pmatrix}.

If we only consider the leading components in eq. (
339
), we can derive the common description for massive vector at IR. After normalization, we find the polarization vector as

\displaystyle\varepsilon_{h=-1}=\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}},\quad\varepsilon_{h=0}=\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}},\quad\varepsilon_{h=+1}=\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{2}}.

(343)

In the SM, only the
t=0
massive vectors couple to other particles, so
t=\pm 1
states should be generated by chirality flip. For example, we act momentum on the state with
h=t=+1
and get

\displaystyle\mathbf{p}\circ(\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}})=-m\lambda_{\alpha}\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}.

(344)

The transversality is flipped to
0
.

On the other hand, we can only use two-component spinors and their complex conjugation to describe the massive vector. If we begin with
|t|=1
, the construction is similar to the Majorana fermion. For example, the
t=-1
massive vector can give

\displaystyle u_{h=-1}^{M}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}\\
-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\eta^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta^{*}_{\alpha_{1}}\eta^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}\end{pmatrix},\quad u_{h=0}^{M}=\begin{pmatrix}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}-\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\eta^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}-\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}\\
-\lambda^{*}_{\alpha_{1}}\eta^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}-\eta^{*}_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}\end{pmatrix},\quad u_{h=+1}^{M}=\begin{pmatrix}\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\eta_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}\\
\lambda^{*}_{\alpha_{1}}\lambda^{*}_{\alpha_{2}}\end{pmatrix}.

(345)

In this case, a massive vector can be represented by only the
(0,\frac{1}{2})
spinors.

Appendix D
The Young diagram formulation of single-particle states

In this section, we introduce a new formulation of single-particle states and wave functions, realized by the semi-standard Young diagrams. The Young diagrams are used to label both the
SU(2)
LG representations and the
SO(2)\times SO(3,1)
reps, with the building blocks given by

\begin{split}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{I},\quad\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt\sim\lambda_{\alpha}^{I},\end{split}

(354)

where each box represents an
SU(2)
index
I
and a spinor index
\alpha
or
\dot{\alpha}
, and the color distinguishes the transversality.

The generic Young diagram consists of at most two rows, and the orange boxes are always placed ahead of the black ones,
15
15

15

The requirement is for each row, so there is a possibility that
\tilde{n}_{1}<\tilde{n}_{2}
, where some black boxes are placed on the top of some orange ones.

height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\makebox[0.5pt][l]{$\smash{\underbrace{\phantom{\begin{matrix}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt&\cdots&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt&\cdots&\hbox{}\hskip height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt\end{matrix}}}_{\text{ $n_{2}$}}}$}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}&\cdots&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}&\cdots&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}&&\end{array}}\\
\\
\sim&\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}^{(I_{1}}\cdots\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{\tilde{n}_{1}}}^{I_{\tilde{n}_{1}}}\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}^{I_{\tilde{n}_{1}+1}}\cdots\lambda_{\alpha_{n_{1}}}^{I_{\tilde{n}_{1}+n_{1}})}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\beta}_{1}I_{1}}\cdots\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\beta}_{\tilde{n}_{2}}I_{\tilde{n}_{2}}}\lambda_{\beta_{1}I_{\tilde{n}_{2}+1}}\cdots\lambda_{\beta_{n_{2}}I_{\tilde{n}_{2}+n_{2}}},\\
&\mbox{with }t=\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{1}-n_{2}}{2},s=\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+n_{1}-\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{2}}{2}.\quad\end{split}

(355)

It can be read from the structure that there are
(\tilde{n}_{1}+n_{1}-\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{2})
permuted uncontracted
SU(2)
indices, corresponding to spin-
\left(\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+n_{1}-\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{2}}{2}\right)
structures. The transversality is obtained by subtracting the number of black boxes
(n_{1}+n_{2})
from the number of orange boxes
(\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2})
, resulting in
\left(\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{1}-n_{2}}{2}\right)
transversality.

The permutation of the
SU(2)
indices would be transferred to the spinor indices, such that the Young diagram represents both the representation of
SU(2)
and the one of
SO(2)\times SO(3,1)
. Therefore, a Young diagram denotes an induced representation of
ISO(2)\times ISO(3,1)
from the
SU(2)
LG.

After building the correspondence between the Young diagram and spinor structures, now we discuss the
SO(2)\times SO(3,1)
representation with the one-row Young diagram

\begin{split}[t,j_{1},j_{2}]=\left[\frac{\tilde{n}-n}{2},\frac{n}{2},\frac{\tilde{n}}{2}\right]\quad\begin{array}[]{cccccc}\makebox[0.5pt][l]{$\smash{\underbrace{\phantom{\begin{matrix}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\ &\ldots{}&\ {\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\end{matrix}}}_{\text{ $\tilde{n}$}}}$}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\ldots&\ {\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\makebox[0.5pt][l]{$\smash{\underbrace{\phantom{\begin{matrix}\hbox{}\hskip height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt&\ \dots{}\ &\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\\
&&&&&\end{array}\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}^{(I_{1}}\cdots\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{\tilde{n}}}^{I_{\tilde{n}}}\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}^{I_{\tilde{n}+1}}\cdots\lambda_{\alpha_{n}}^{I_{\tilde{n}+n})},\end{split}

(356)

which is also a spin-
\left(\frac{n+\tilde{n}}{2}\right)
wave function. The relationship between the wave function and its field is

\begin{split}\Psi_{(\dot{\alpha}_{1}\cdots\dot{\alpha}_{\tilde{n}})(\alpha_{1}\cdots\alpha_{n})}=\int\frac{d^{4}\mathbf{p}}{(2\pi)^{4}}\delta(\mathbf{p}^{2}-\mathbf{m}^{2})\Big(&\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}}^{(I_{1}}\cdots\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{\tilde{n}}}^{I_{\tilde{n}}}\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}^{I_{\tilde{n}+1}}\cdots\lambda_{\alpha_{n}}^{I_{\tilde{n}+n})}a_{I_{1}\cdots I_{\tilde{n}+n}}e^{-i\mathbf{p}\cdot x}\\
&+\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{1}(I_{1}}\cdots\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}_{\tilde{n}}I_{\tilde{n}}}\lambda_{\alpha_{1}I_{\tilde{n}+1}}\cdots\lambda_{\alpha_{n}I_{\tilde{n}+n})}(a^{\dagger})^{I_{1}\cdots I_{\tilde{n}+n}}e^{i\mathbf{p}\cdot x}\Big),\end{split}

(357)

where
a
and
a^{\dagger}
are the annihilating and creating operators of a particle.

The two-row structures like eq. (
355
) involve contraction of the
SU(2)
indices, leading to factors of the 6D momentum

\begin{split}p_{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}m\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}&-\mathbf{p}_{\beta\dot{\alpha}}\\
\mathbf{p}_{\alpha\dot{\beta}}&-\tilde{m}\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}}\end{pmatrix},\end{split}

(358)

so they are single-particle states instead of wave functions.
Specifically, the one-column-two-row structures are

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}}

\displaystyle\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{I_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\beta}I_{1}}=-\tilde{m}\tilde{\epsilon}_{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}},

\displaystyle\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}

\displaystyle\sim\lambda_{\alpha}^{I_{1}}\lambda_{\beta I_{1}}=m\epsilon_{\alpha\beta},

(359)

\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{c}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\\
\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\end{array}

\displaystyle\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{I_{1}}\lambda_{\beta I_{1}}=-\mathbf{p}_{\beta\dot{\alpha}},

\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{c}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\\
{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\end{array}

\displaystyle\sim\lambda_{\alpha}^{I_{1}}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\beta}I_{1}}=\mathbf{p}_{\alpha\dot{\beta}}.

\sim&\begin{cases}\mathop{\bigoplus}\limits_{0\leq k\leq n_{1}-n_{2}}\begin{cases}\left[\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{1}-n_{2}}{2},\frac{n_{1}-n_{2}}{2},\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}-\tilde{n}_{2}+2(k-n_{2})}{2}\right]&k\geq n_{2}\\

\mathop{\bigoplus}\limits_{0\leq k\leq\tilde{n}_{1}-\tilde{n}_{2}}\begin{cases}\left[\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{1}-n_{2}}{2},\frac{n_{1}-n_{2}}{2},\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2}-2k}{2}\right]&k<\tilde{n}_{2}\\
\left[\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}+\tilde{n}_{2}-n_{1}-n_{2}}{2},\frac{n_{1}-n_{2}+2(k-\tilde{n}_{2})}{2},\frac{\tilde{n}_{1}-\tilde{n}_{2}}{2}\right]&k\geq\tilde{n}_{2}\end{cases}&\tilde{n}_{1}\geq\tilde{n}_{2}\end{cases}\end{split}

(360)

which is inferred from the correspondence between the Young diagram and its spinor structure given by eq. (
355
). For example,

\begin{split}\begin{array}[]{ccc}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\\

(362)

The single-particle state
|t,s,h\rangle
can be obtained by filling the Young tableau of the irreducible representation
[t,j_{1},j_{2}]
with appropriate values. There are only two possible values,
+
and
-
, corresponding to the
SU(2)
states
\zeta^{+I}
and
\zeta^{-I}
respectively:

\begin{split}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}\zeta^{+I},\ {\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}\sim\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\zeta^{-I},\\
\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt\sim-\lambda_{\alpha}\zeta^{-I},\ \hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt\sim\eta_{\alpha}\zeta^{+I}.\end{split}

(363)

The rule for filling the Young tableau, subject to the constraints of Young’s orthogonality relations, requires that
+
always appears to the left of
-
in each row, and no column can contain repeated values.

We illustrate the Young tableau using examples for spin-1, showing how the states are arranged according to Young’s orthogonality relations. The
[t,j_{1},j_{2}]=\left[-1,1,0\right]
representation with all possible helicity states is given by

\begin{split}\begin{tabular}[]{ccl}$h=+1$&$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$&$\sim\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}^{(+}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}^{+)}=\eta_{(\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2})}\zeta^{+(I_{1}}\zeta^{+I_{2})}$,\\
$h=0$&$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$&$\sim\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}^{(+}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}^{-)}=-\lambda_{(\alpha_{1}}\eta_{\alpha_{2})}\zeta^{+(I_{1}}\zeta^{-I_{2})}$,\\
$h=-1$&$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$&$\sim\lambda_{\alpha_{1}}^{(-}\lambda_{\alpha_{2}}^{-)}=\lambda_{(\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{\alpha_{2})}\zeta^{-(I_{1}}\zeta^{-I_{2})}$.\end{tabular}\end{split}

(364)

where
\begin{cases}\lambda_{\alpha}^{+}\equiv\eta_{\alpha}\zeta^{+I}\\
\lambda_{\alpha}^{-}\equiv-\lambda_{\alpha}\zeta^{-I}\end{cases}
labels the components of the little group index
I
.
Similarly, the helicity states of
\left[0,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}\right]
are given by

\begin{split}\begin{tabular}[]{ccl}$h=+1$&$\begin{array}[]{cc}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\end{array}$&$\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{(+}\lambda_{\alpha}^{+)}=\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}\eta_{\alpha}\zeta^{+(I_{1}}\zeta^{+I_{2})}$,\\
$h=0$&$\begin{array}[]{cc}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$+$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\end{array}$&$\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{(+}\lambda_{\alpha}^{-)}=(\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\eta_{\alpha}-\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}\lambda_{\alpha})\zeta^{+(I_{1}}\zeta^{-I_{2})}$,\\
$h=-1$&$\begin{array}[]{cc}{\color[rgb]{1,0.5,0}\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt}&\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt\hbox to10.93333pt{\hfil$-$\hfil}\vrule height=8.74669pt,width=0.3pt,depth=2.18663pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\end{array}$&$\sim\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{(-}\lambda_{\alpha}^{-)}=-\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\lambda_{\alpha}\zeta^{-(I_{1}}\zeta^{-I_{2})}$.\end{tabular}\end{split}

(365)

where
\begin{cases}\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{+}\equiv\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}\zeta^{+I}\\
\tilde{\lambda}_{\dot{\alpha}}^{-}\equiv\tilde{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\zeta^{-I}\end{cases}
